text:
The Rangers lost Igor Shesterkin for the season in October, and their net has been a running story ever since: James Reimer's comeback ended with his contract terminated, Dylan Garand has taken 14 of 21 starts, and tonight Joonas Korpisalo, back from a long stint on injured reserve, gets the crease against Montreal. The New York Post says they've finally found a balance with the Korpisalo and Garand pairing. The skaters in front of them have made that easier. The Rangers have won the chance battle in all five of their last five games, with 60% of the expected goals (the quality of the chances), and went 4-1 doing it, finishing the trip with a 5-1 win in Vancouver.

Montreal is the opposite kind of good. The Canadiens have 28 points, three more than the Rangers, but their results are well ahead of their chances: a +5 goal difference on -4.7 expected. Jacob Fowler is the reason. He's at +13.5 goals saved above expected in 12 games, .926 overall, and 3-0-2 with 3.6 saved above expected over his last five starts. That's a goalie holding a team up, and Saturday's 4-1 loss to Colorado, when Montreal managed just 31% of the expected goals, showed what happens when even that isn't enough.

The Habs are also thin. Ivan Demidov (ankle) didn't travel and isn't expected back until about Nov 21, Chris Kreider is on injured reserve until January, and Mike Matheson and Josh Anderson picked up lower-body injuries this weekend. Oliver Kapanen has taken Demidov's spot beside Juraj Slafkovsky and Alex Newhook, and Zachary Bolduc is now on the top power play. Slafkovsky is the one to watch: no goals in eleven games on 3.8 expected, the kind of drought chances usually end.

On the other side, Cole Caufield arrives on a six-game point streak and Mika Zibanejad on a five-gamer after climbing the Rangers' record book in Calgary. Our numbers lean slightly to the Rangers' chances, 3.34 expected goals to 2.99. Montreal's 4.9 penalties a game against a power play that makes 0.73 expected goals a night is where we'd look first.
headline: Fowler's wall meets a Rangers team winning the ice
